In Unix-based systems:
```
ps aux | grep python
```
This command will show you a list of all the running Python processes and their PIDs.

In Windows:
```
tasklist | findstr python
```
This command will show you a list of all the running Python processes and their PIDs.

Once you have the PID of the Python process you want to kill, you can use the `kill` command in Unix-based systems or the `taskkill` command in Windows to stop the process.

In Unix-based systems:
```
kill -2 <PID>
```
Replace `<PID>` with the actual process ID.

In Windows:
```
taskkill /F /PID <PID>
```
Replace `<PID>` with the actual process ID.

The `-2` flag in Unix-based systems and the `/F` flag in Windows both forcefully terminate the process.
